session_read: Fresh intraday sweep, then a second pass after the first attempt lost its entire analyst layer to a platform-wide API outage. All four analysts and the strategist have since completed, so this run is no longer degraded on the judgment side -- only smith-signals remains partial, and its gaps are labelled rather than filled in. The book was rebuilt today: 32 names from 28, ~$7.5k deployed across 12 buys in a 50-minute window after the open, plus two stop-loss sells. All 15 trades carry an exact email-confirmed fill and a stated reason. Cash fell 22.5% to 7.33% and is back inside its band; the AI Networking/Optics underweight was cured outright; drawdown healed from -6.04% to -3.82%. The cost was specific: aggregate open risk rose from 9.77% to 12.44% against a 10% cap, and names over their own ATR cap went from five to nine. Of today's +$7,317, only $2,274 was market move. The proposal engine now answers the brief it was given. Five of eleven open ideas are driven by the new non-ATR triggers, and two of the three HIGH-priority slots are profit-booking rather than cap repair. Two self-funding rotations stand ready at zero deployable cash -- BX into GE Vernova, and NVDA's existing trim into Qualcomm -- alongside two stop-ratchets that protect roughly $218 of unrealised gain for no cash at all. A third rotation, Microsoft into Meta, is deliberately held: Meta's thesis was resolved to intact this run and it is the book's only oversold name, but a stale headwind flag still blocks it and the agent that could clear it was the one that failed. Nebius, up 20.6%, is now explained -- a genuine Q2 beat plus a billion-dollar compute contract -- so its risk-cap breach rests on real information, which argues for ratcheting the stop rather than trimming. IREN, by contrast, is a chase: no catalyst since the watermark, and the cash it would need is operating buffer, not dry powder.
